key_insight: Two deep neural networks perform inverse design for bosonic quantum hardware by directly mapping target cavity or qubit parameters to candidate SRF cavity and transmon geometries.
engineering_relevance: This can dramatically reduce the trial-and-error simulation burden in designing long-lived cavity-transmon systems for scalable bosonic quantum computation.
method: DNN #1 proposes SRF cavity geometries from target cavity observables.
DNN #2 proposes transmon designs from target coupling rate, qubit frequency, and anharmonicity targets.
Candidate designs are re-simulated end-to-end to verify performance.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports recovered designs matching targets to within about 5% for cavities and 2% for transmons after re-simulation.
watch_item: Inverse design remains one-to-many, so practical deployment will still need careful validation of manufacturability, robustness, and sensitivity to fabrication tolerances.
paper_title: Neural-Network Inverse Design of SRF Cavities and Transmons for Bosonic Quantum Computation
